intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the magical hanami tradition under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Pack a picnic, join locals in celebrating the fleeting beauty of sakura, and stroll the lantern-lit paths in the evening. Families can enjoy street food stalls selling takoyaki and dango around the park perimeter.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple in the historic Asakusa district. Walk through the Thunder Gate (Kaminarimon), explore the vibrant Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts and snacks, and participate in omikuji fortune-drawing. A deeply immersive cultural and historical experience perfect for families.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A profoundly moving and educational experience for families, the Peace Memorial Museum chronicles the events of August 6, 1945 with powerful exhibits and personal stories. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, see the iconic A-Bomb Dome, and fold origami cranes at the Children's Peace Monument. Essential historical context for understanding modern Japan.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Japanese culinary culture at the world-famous Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, and matcha treats from dozens of stalls. Join a guided family-friendly food tour to learn about Japanese ingredients, cooking traditions, and the art of sushi-making from local vendors.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Wander through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most iconic natural and cultural landscapes. Extend the adventure with a visit to Iwatayama Monkey Park, where children can hand-feed Japanese macaques with panoramic views of Kyoto below. Combine with a rickshaw ride through the historic district for a full family day.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage. Take the affordable airport limousine bus or train to your accommodation (Aegean Bliss Resort). Check in, freshen up, and rest.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick and cheap bite at the airport convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) — onigiri rice balls and instant noodles are filling and cost under ¥500. Many airport food stalls are open late.

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first night stress-free. Buy a prepaid IC card (Suica or Pasmo) at the airport for easy transit payments throughout the trip. Also consider picking up a budget data SIM card or pocket Wi-Fi rental at the airport arrival hall.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in to recover from jet lag. After a slow start, head to a nearby local breakfast spot or convenience store for a traditional Japanese morning meal. Explore the immediate neighborhood around the resort — walk along the beachfront, get oriented, and soak in the surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local market or shopping street to pick up essentials and snacks for the trip. Browse 100-yen shops (Daiso) for affordable souvenirs and supplies. Take a relaxing stroll and enjoy the coastal scenery near the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a casual dinner at a nearby ramen or gyudon (beef bowl) restaurant. Yoshinoya or Matsuya chains offer hearty meals for under ¥600. Return to the resort early to rest and plan the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast (onigiri, tamagoyaki egg roll, miso soup cup) — approx ¥400–600
meals.lunch: Local soba or udon noodle shop near the resort — approx ¥700–900
meals.dinner: Gyudon beef bowl at Yoshinoya or Sukiya chain restaurant — approx ¥500–700

day_by_day.notes: Use this day as a gentle recovery and orientation day. Download Google Maps offline for your region and bookmark key transport hubs. Check cherry blossom forecast updates — mid-April is typically peak or late bloom season.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Tokyo's Asakusa district via public transit. Visit Senso-ji Temple, Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple. Arrive early (before 9am) to beat crowds. Explore the temple grounds, wash hands at the purification fountain, and draw an omikuji fortune slip (¥100).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Nakamise Shopping Street, the vibrant 250-meter arcade leading to Senso-ji. Browse affordable traditional crafts, snacks like ningyo-yaki cakes and senbei crackers, and budget souvenirs. Cross the nearby Azuma Bridge for great views of the Tokyo Skytree. Explore Asakusa's side streets and the Hoppy Street area.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Asakusa at a budget izakaya (Japanese pub) or a tempura rice bowl (tendon) restaurant. Try Kaminarimon area eateries. Head back to the resort via train.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — approx ¥400–600
meals.lunch: Street food along Nakamise Street — ningyo-yaki, melonpan, yakitori skewers — approx ¥600–800
meals.dinner: Tendon (tempura rice bowl) at a local Asakusa restaurant — approx ¥800–1,100

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter. Nakamise Shopping Street is great for budget souvenir shopping — prices are more competitive here than at tourist trap shops. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The temple is beautiful at dusk if you have time.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Shinkansen or express train to Kyoto (budget tip: book JR Pass in advance or use discount Shinkansen tickets). Arrive in Kyoto mid-morning. Head straight to Maruyama Park for the iconic Cherry Blossom Viewing (Hanami). Experience the magical weeping cherry tree — one of Japan's most celebrated — in full bloom.
day_by_day.afternoon: After hanami, explore the adjacent Yasaka Shrine (free entry) and stroll through the charming Gion district, Kyoto's famous geisha quarter. Walk along Hanamikoji Street and browse traditional machiya townhouses. Visit Kennin-ji Temple (¥500 entry), Kyoto's oldest Zen temple, nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner at Nishiki Market — known as 'Kyoto's Kitchen' — for affordable street food tastings: tofu skewers, pickles, tamagoyaki. Return to your accommodation or consider an overnight budget hostel in Kyoto to save on transport the next day.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — approx ¥400–600
meals.lunch: Bento box or onigiri picnic under the cherry blossoms in Maruyama Park — approx ¥600–800
meals.dinner: Street food tasting at Nishiki Market — approx ¥800–1,200

day_by_day.notes: Mid-April cherry blossoms in Kyoto may be at late bloom or petal-fall stage — still beautiful. Bring a picnic mat for hanami. Maruyama Park is free to enter. Book Shinkansen tickets in advance for best prices. A JR Pass can be very cost-effective if traveling between multiple cities.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and head to Arashiyama district in western Kyoto. Walk through the ethereal Arashiyama Bamboo Grove (free, open 24 hours) — most magical and least crowded before 8am. Explore the surrounding Tenryu-ji Temple garden (¥500 garden entry) with its stunning pond and mountain backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park (¥550 for adults, ¥250 for children) for panoramic views of Kyoto and close encounters with Japanese macaque monkeys — a fantastic family activity. Afterward, stroll along the Togetsukyo Bridge and browse the Arashiyama shopping street for affordable snacks and crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Take the scenic Sagano Romantic Train (¥880 one-way) through the Hozu River gorge if budget allows, or simply enjoy the riverside at dusk. Dinner in Arashiyama before returning to accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or local bakery in Arashiyama — approx ¥400–600
meals.lunch: Yudofu (tofu hot pot) set meal at an Arashiyama restaurant — approx ¥900–1,200
meals.dinner: Ramen or soba at a local Arashiyama eatery — approx ¥700–1,000

day_by_day.notes: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is free but gets very crowded by mid-morning — arrive before 8am for the best experience. The Monkey Park involves a 20-minute uphill hike — wear comfortable shoes. Great for families with children. Bring cash as some smaller vendors don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Kyoto to Hiroshima via Shinkansen (covered by JR Pass or approx ¥5,500 one-way). Arrive in Hiroshima and check in to a budget guesthouse or hostel. Head to the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum (¥200 entry — extremely affordable) for a profoundly moving and educational experience about the 1945 atomic bombing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the adjacent Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park (free). Visit the iconic A-Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Walk along the park's memorials including the Children's Peace Monument and the Flame of Peace. Reflect and spend meaningful time with family.
day_by_day.evening: Try Hiroshima's famous local specialty: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (savory layered pancake) — distinctly different from Osaka-style and a must-eat. Okonomimura (Okonomiyaki Village) building has multiple floors of affordable vendors. Return to accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store en route to station — approx ¥400–600
meals.lunch: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki near the Peace Park — approx ¥800–1,100
meals.dinner: Okonomimura Okonomiyaki Village — approx ¥900–1,200

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum is one of the most important cultural and historical sites in Japan — deeply moving for all ages. Allow at least 2 hours inside. The museum is very child-friendly with clear English signage. ¥200 entry is one of Japan's best-value museum experiences. Bring tissues.

day_by_day.morning: Take the JR Ferry or Sanyo Line to Miyajima Island (ferry approx ¥200 each way, or free with JR Pass). Visit the iconic Itsukushima Shrine and its famous floating torii gate — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore the shrine complex (¥300 entry) and walk along the waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up Mount Misen (free trail or ropeway ¥1,000 one-way) for breathtaking panoramic views of the Seto Inland Sea. Alternatively, explore the island's deer (roaming freely and very tame — great for kids), and visit Daisho-in Temple (free) on the lower slopes. Browse the Omotesando shopping street for momiji manju (maple leaf cakes).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hiroshima by ferry and train. Enjoy a final Hiroshima dinner — try local oysters (Hiroshima is famous for them) at an affordable seafood restaurant near the station. Return to accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or guesthouse breakfast — approx ¥400–600
meals.lunch: Grilled oysters and momiji manju on Miyajima Island — approx ¥800–1,100
meals.dinner: Oyster rice (kaki-meshi) or oyster gratin at a Hiroshima restaurant — approx ¥900–1,300

day_by_day.notes: Miyajima is one of Japan's 'Three Views' — absolutely stunning. The floating torii is best photographed at high tide. Check tide times before visiting. The free-roaming deer are very friendly and popular with children but keep food out of reach. JR Pass covers the JR Ferry to Miyajima — great savings.

day_by_day.morning: Travel back toward the Tokyo/resort area via Shinkansen. If time permits, stop in Osaka for a few hours en route. Explore Dotonbori, Osaka's famous entertainment district — walk along the neon-lit canal and see the iconic Glico Running Man sign. Try takoyaki (octopus balls) fresh from street stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Osaka's Shinsekai district for retro atmosphere and budget kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers) — the local specialty. Visit Den Den Town (Osaka's electronics/anime district) for affordable manga, anime goods, and retro gaming. Then board the Shinkansen back toward Tokyo/resort.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at resort area. Enjoy a quiet evening, do laundry, repack, and review photos and memories from the trip. Grab dinner at a nearby chain restaurant or convenience store.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store at Hiroshima Station — approx ¥400–600
meals.lunch: Osaka street food: takoyaki, okonomiyaki, taiyaki — approx ¥700–1,000
meals.dinner: Kushikatsu at Shinsekai or convenience store dinner at resort — approx ¥800–1,100

day_by_day.notes: Osaka is a fantastic food city and very budget-friendly. Even a 3–4 hour layover gives you enough time to experience Dotonbori and grab street food. Luggage storage is available at Osaka Station (approx ¥500–700 per locker). Keep Shinkansen tickets handy for platform access.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Tokyo for a final city exploration day. Visit Ueno Park — one of Tokyo's largest public parks and a famous cherry blossom spot (late petals may still be visible). Explore the Ueno Zoo (¥600 for adults, ¥200 for children) — Japan's oldest zoo and a great family activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno (¥1,000 entry) — Japan's largest museum with extensive collections of Japanese art, samurai armor, ceramics, and cultural artifacts. Perfect for history and culture enthusiasts. Alternatively, explore the free Ueno Tosho-gu Shrine within the park.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Akihabara (Electric Town) for a fun evening browsing multi-floor electronics shops, retro arcades, and anime/manga stores. Enjoy dinner at a budget conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) restaurant — Sushiro or Kura Sushi offer plates from ¥110 each. Return to resort.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — approx ¥400–600
meals.lunch: Ueno Park area lunch — ramen or curry rice at a local restaurant — approx ¥700–1,000
meals.dinner: Conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) in Akihabara — approx ¥1,000–1,500

day_by_day.notes: Ueno Park is free to enter and a beloved hanami spot — even late-season cherry blossoms create a beautiful atmosphere. The Tokyo National Museum is exceptional value for history lovers and has excellent English labeling. Akihabara is exciting for all ages — great for budget gaming and anime souvenir shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and take a last walk along the beachfront near the resort. Pack and check out. If time allows, visit a nearby local shrine or morning market for one last authentic Japanese experience. Pick up any final souvenirs at a nearby 100-yen shop or convenience store.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport with plenty of time (aim to arrive 3 hours before international departure). Use remaining yen on airport food, duty-free shopping, or last-minute snacks for the flight. Return any rented pocket Wi-Fi devices at the airport counter.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Japan. Reflect on 10 incredible days of cherry blossoms, ancient temples, moving history, and unforgettable family memories. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store — approx ¥400–600
meals.lunch: Airport food court — ramen, sushi set, or bento box — approx ¥800–1,200
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for airport check-in and security on departure day. Spend down remaining small yen coins at vending machines or convenience stores — they're hard to exchange abroad. Consider mailing heavier souvenirs home via Japan Post's affordable international parcel service (Yu-Pack) to avoid excess baggage fees. Keep a small amount of yen for train fare to the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival day — no morning activities scheduled. Flight UA arrives at 22:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrival day — no afternoon activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for landing.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to beat jet lag.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport before departure.
meals.lunch: On the plane or at a transit airport.
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite at the airport — try a conveyor belt sushi bar or ramen stand in the arrivals hall before heading to the hotel (budget ¥1,000–¥1,500).

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag is real. Pick up a Suica IC card and pocket Wi-Fi or SIM card at the airport for easy transport and navigation throughout the trip. Exchange some yen at the airport currency counter for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Start gently to recover from jet lag. Enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast, then take a relaxing walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort. Explore the immediate neighborhood, visit a local convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) to stock up on snacks and drinks — a quintessential Japanese experience in itself.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into the nearest city center for orientation. Visit a local shrine or temple in the area to ease into Japanese culture. Browse a nearby shopping district or covered arcade (shotengai) to pick up any essentials. If near Tokyo, consider a gentle visit to a local park to spot late cherry blossoms.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy your first proper sit-down dinner in Japan. Find a mid-range izakaya (Japanese pub-style restaurant) near the hotel for a relaxed family-friendly meal with shared dishes like yakitori, edamame, karaage, and cold beer or soft drinks.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy the included or buffet spread to fuel up (¥0–¥1,500 depending on inclusion).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local soba or udon restaurant near the hotel — try cold zaru soba or warm kitsune udon (budget ¥800–¥1,200 per person).
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner near the hotel — order a variety of small plates to share. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,500 per person including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: This is an acclimatization day. Don't over-schedule — let the family adjust to the time zone. April in Japan is mild and pleasant (15–22°C), perfect for light outdoor exploration. Keep the day flexible and low-pressure.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Tokyo (by shinkansen or local express if not already there). Head to Asakusa district and begin the day at Senso-ji Temple — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple. Arrive early (by 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Admire the Kaminarimon Thunder Gate, walk through the lantern-lined Nakamise Shopping Street, and explore the temple grounds. Let kids toss coins and ring the bell for good luck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along Nakamise Shopping Street to browse traditional Japanese souvenirs — ningyo dolls, fans, keychains, and matcha sweets. Then walk to the nearby Sumida River waterfront for beautiful views of Tokyo Skytree. If cherry blossoms are still blooming, Sumida Park along the river is a gorgeous hanami spot with hundreds of sakura trees.
day_by_day.evening: Take the metro to Akihabara for a family-friendly evening exploring Japan's famous electronics and anime district. Browse multi-floor arcades, retro game shops, and themed cafes. Enjoy dinner at a lively restaurant in the area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab an onigiri and hot coffee from a convenience store on the way to the station (budget ¥300–¥500).
meals.lunch: Lunch near Senso-ji — try a tempura donburi (tendon) set at a local restaurant in Asakusa (budget ¥1,200–¥1,800 per person).
meals.dinner: Akihabara dinner at a mid-range curry house or ramen shop — try Japanese-style curry rice (kare raisu) which is a family favorite (budget ¥1,000–¥1,800 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter. Nakamise Shopping Street is a great spot to buy early souvenirs. Wear comfortable shoes — lots of walking today. If traveling with young children, the Sumida Park hanami area has open grassy spaces to run around.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in Tokyo. Start the morning at the Tsukiji Outer Market for an immersive Japanese culinary culture experience. Arrive by 8:00–9:00 AM when stalls are freshest and most active. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet egg omelet), grilled seafood skewers, and freshly brewed green tea as you wander the bustling lanes.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market, make your way to Hamarikyu Gardens nearby — a beautiful traditional Japanese garden with a teahouse on a tidal pond. Enjoy matcha tea and wagashi sweets in the teahouse. Then head to Shibuya or Shinjuku for afternoon exploration — visit Shibuya Crossing (the world's busiest pedestrian scramble), browse Tokyu Hands or Don Quijote for unique Japanese goods.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sunset views from a free observation point — the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building in Shinjuku offers free panoramic views of the city. Then wind down with dinner in Shinjuku's Memory Lane (Omoide Yokocho) — a narrow alley of tiny yakitori stalls with incredible atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market food tour breakfast — graze on fresh sushi, oysters, tamagoyaki, and street snacks (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Hamarikyu Gardens teahouse — matcha and wagashi set (budget ¥800–¥1,200 per person) or a nearby bento from a convenience store.
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) in Shinjuku — small skewers of yakitori, grilled vegetables, and cold Sapporo beer in a lantern-lit alley (budget ¥2,000–¥3,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is free to walk through — just budget for food purchases. Hamarikyu Gardens charges a small entry fee (¥300 adults, ¥150 children). The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observatory is free and offers stunning city views, especially at dusk. Omoide Yokocho is very atmospheric but stalls are small — arrive by 6:00 PM to get seats.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Tokaido Shinkansen (bullet train) from Tokyo to Kyoto — approximately 2 hours 15 minutes on the Hikari or Nozomi service. Arrive in Kyoto mid-morning. Check in to luggage storage at Kyoto Station and head directly to Arashiyama district. Walk through the ethereal Arashiyama Bamboo Grove — a stunning tunnel of towering green bamboo stalks that filter light magically in the morning hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Bamboo Grove, visit Tenryu-ji Temple and its UNESCO-listed garden (¥500 entry). Then take the optional hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park — kids will love interacting with over 120 wild Japanese macaques with panoramic views of Kyoto below (¥550 entry). Explore the charming Arashiyama riverside and browse artisan shops along Togetsukyo Bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Kyoto and check in to your accommodation for the Kyoto portion of the trip. Explore the Gion district in the evening — stroll the atmospheric Hanamikoji Street where you may spot geiko or maiko (geisha apprentices) heading to evening engagements.

meals.breakfast: Grab a shinkansen bento (ekiben) from the Tokyo Station food hall before boarding — a classic Japanese travel tradition (budget ¥1,000–¥1,500).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Arashiyama — try yudofu (tofu hot pot) at a riverside restaurant, a Kyoto specialty (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person).
meals.dinner: Gion district dinner at a mid-range kaiseki-style set meal restaurant or a casual obanzai (Kyoto home cooking) restaurant — small seasonal vegetable dishes, tofu, and grilled fish (budget ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book shinkansen tickets in advance — use the JR Pass if it covers your route for significant savings. The Bamboo Grove is best visited early morning to avoid crowds. Monkey Park requires a moderate uphill walk — manageable for most families with children over 5. Gion evening walks are free and magical.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for the highlight of the trip — Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park. Head to Kyoto's most famous hanami spot by 8:00 AM to experience the magical weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) in the soft morning light before crowds arrive. Spread a picnic blanket under the blossoms for a traditional hanami experience. The park is free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Maruyama Park to the nearby Yasaka Shrine, then continue to Kiyomizudera Temple — one of Kyoto's most iconic landmarks perched on a wooden stage overlooking the city (¥500 entry). Stroll down the charming Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka stone-paved lanes lined with traditional shops selling Kyoto crafts, ceramics, and matcha sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine for the early evening — the thousands of vermillion torii gates leading up the mountain are breathtaking at dusk. Walk as far as the family is comfortable (even the first 20 minutes is spectacular). Return to Kyoto city center for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Picnic breakfast in Maruyama Park — pick up onigiri, sandwiches, and drinks from a convenience store the night before (budget ¥500–¥800 per person).
meals.lunch: Lunch on Ninenzaka or Sannenzaka — try a matcha parfait and a light meal at one of the charming cafes (budget ¥1,200–¥2,000 per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner in central Kyoto near Kawaramachi — try a shabu-shabu or sukiyaki restaurant where you cook thinly sliced beef in a communal pot at the table, a fun family dining experience (budget ¥3,000–¥4,500 per person).

day_by_day.notes: April 20 is peak cherry blossom season — Maruyama Park will be stunning. Arrive early to secure a good spot under the weeping cherry tree. Kiyomizudera can be very crowded by midday — visit right after Maruyama if possible. Fushimi Inari is free to enter and open 24 hours. Wear comfortable walking shoes — today involves significant uphill walking.

day_by_day.morning: Explore more of Kyoto's incredible cultural heritage. Start with the Golden Pavilion — Kinkaku-ji Temple (¥500 entry) — one of Japan's most photographed landmarks, its gold-leaf exterior reflecting perfectly in the surrounding pond. Then visit the nearby Ryoan-ji Temple to contemplate Japan's most famous Zen rock garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Nijo Castle (¥1,030 entry) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and former residence of the Tokugawa shoguns. Explore the ornate Ninomaru Palace with its famous 'nightingale floors' that chirp when walked upon (a historic security system). The castle gardens are beautiful with late cherry blossoms. This is a particularly engaging history experience for families.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening at Nishiki Market — Kyoto's narrow covered market street nicknamed 'Kyoto's Kitchen.' Sample pickled vegetables, fresh tofu, grilled skewers, and local street food as you browse 100+ stalls. Then enjoy a relaxed dinner nearby in the Kawaramachi entertainment district.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a traditional Japanese breakfast set at a local kissaten (old-school coffee shop) — rice, miso soup, grilled fish, and pickles (budget ¥800–¥1,200).
meals.lunch: Lunch near Nijo Castle — try a teishoku (set meal) at a local restaurant with rice, soup, and multiple small dishes (budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner in Kawaramachi — try a mid-range tonkatsu restaurant (breaded pork cutlet with cabbage and miso soup), a crowd-pleasing family option (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Kinkaku-ji is extremely popular — go right when it opens at 9:00 AM. Nijo Castle's nightingale floors are a fascinating piece of history that children find particularly memorable. Nishiki Market closes around 6:00 PM, so plan the evening visit accordingly. Keep receipts for tax-free shopping if spending over ¥5,000 at eligible stores.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hiroshima — take the Shinkansen from Kyoto to Hiroshima (approximately 1 hour 20 minutes). Head directly to the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park — a profoundly moving and educational experience for families. The museum chronicles the events of August 6, 1945, with powerful exhibits, personal artifacts, and survivor testimonies. Allow 2–3 hours for a thorough visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the museum, walk through the Peace Memorial Park and see the iconic A-Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome) — the skeletal ruins of the former Industrial Promotion Hall, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Pay respects at the Children's Peace Monument and fold a paper crane in honor of Sadako Sasaki. Then take the ferry to Miyajima Island to see the famous floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine at high tide.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Miyajima Island — walk along the waterfront, encounter friendly deer roaming freely, and visit Itsukushima Shrine (¥300 entry). Watch the torii gate glow at dusk. Take the ferry back to Hiroshima and catch the Shinkansen back to Kyoto for the night.

meals.breakfast: Shinkansen bento from Kyoto Station — pick up a Kyoto-style obento before boarding (budget ¥1,000–¥1,500).
meals.lunch: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki near the Peace Park — Hiroshima's famous savory pancake layered with noodles, cabbage, and egg is a must-try local specialty (budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person).
meals.dinner: Quick dinner at Hiroshima Station before the return Shinkansen — try oysters (Hiroshima is famous for them) at a station restaurant, or pick up a Hiroshima bento for the train (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum is deeply sobering — prepare children aged 8+ with age-appropriate context beforehand. Entry is ¥200 for adults, free for children. The museum is one of the most important historical sites in the world and should not be rushed. Miyajima ferry is covered by JR Pass. Check tide times in advance — the floating torii is most dramatic at high tide.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Tokyo/hotel area region. Take the Shinkansen back toward your base. If time allows before departure, visit one more Kyoto highlight — the Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku no Michi), a 2km stone path along a canal lined with hundreds of cherry trees. In late April some blossoms may still linger, and the walk is peaceful and beautiful. Pass by Nanzen-ji Temple along the route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back at your hotel base. Use the afternoon for leisure, souvenir shopping, and packing. Visit a nearby department store basement food hall (depachika) — a Japanese institution offering premium prepared foods, sweets, and gift sets. Stock up on omiyage (souvenir gifts) for friends and family back home — Japanese Kit Kat flavors, wagashi, and regional snacks make perfect gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a celebratory farewell dinner at a slightly elevated restaurant — try a teppanyaki restaurant where skilled chefs cook Wagyu beef, seafood, and vegetables on an iron griddle right at your table. A memorable, interactive dining experience perfect for the final evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick convenience store breakfast before checking out of Kyoto accommodation (budget ¥300–¥800).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a soba restaurant along the Philosopher's Path or near Nanzen-ji — try hot soba noodle soup in a traditional setting (budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person).
meals.dinner: Farewell teppanyaki dinner — mid-range teppanyaki set with Wagyu beef, vegetables, fried rice, and miso soup (budget ¥4,000–¥6,000 per person). Book in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The Philosopher's Path is free to walk. Nanzen-ji Temple grounds are free (some sub-temples charge ¥500). Depachika shopping is a highlight of Japanese food culture — even browsing is an experience. For omiyage, Tokyo Banana, Shiroi Koibito (if you visited Hokkaido), and regional wagashi are always well-received. Confirm departure logistics for Day 10.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Japan. Wake up early for one last Japanese experience — visit a local neighborhood shotengai (covered shopping street) or morning market near the hotel. Enjoy a peaceful final breakfast and take a slow walk to soak in the atmosphere. If near a park, enjoy one last look at the cherry blossoms (late April may still offer some blooms or beautiful green leaves).
day_by_day.afternoon: Complete final packing and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Head to the airport with plenty of time — allow 3 hours before international departure. At the airport, explore the duty-free shops for last-minute gifts and Japanese whisky, cosmetics, or snacks. Enjoy a final meal at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Board your departing flight. Reflect on an incredible 10 days in Japan — from the serenity of cherry blossoms in Maruyama Park to the solemnity of Hiroshima, the electric energy of Tokyo to the timeless beauty of Kyoto's temples.

meals.breakfast: Final Japanese breakfast — visit a local kissaten or hotel restaurant for a classic morning set with coffee, toast, egg, and salad, or a Japanese-style breakfast with rice and miso soup (budget ¥800–¥1,500).
meals.lunch: Airport lunch at one of the terminal restaurants — Japanese airports have excellent dining options including ramen, sushi conveyor belts, and tempura sets (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person).
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dinner depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Return your Suica IC card at the airport for a refund of remaining balance (minus a ¥220 handling fee). Return pocket Wi-Fi device at the airport rental counter. Keep all receipts for tax-free purchases — you may need to show them at customs. Japan's consumption tax refund for tourists applies to purchases over ¥5,000 at participating stores. Safe travels — sayonara Japan!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the magical hanami tradition under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Pack a picnic, join locals in celebrating the fleeting beauty of sakura, and stroll the lantern-lit paths in the evening. Families can enjoy street food stalls selling takoyaki and dango around the park perimeter.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple in the historic Asakusa district. Walk through the Thunder Gate (Kaminarimon), explore the vibrant Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts and snacks, and participate in omikuji fortune-drawing. A deeply immersive cultural and historical experience perfect for families.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A profoundly moving and educational experience for families, the Peace Memorial Museum chronicles the events of August 6, 1945 with powerful exhibits and personal stories. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, see the iconic A-Bomb Dome, and fold origami cranes at the Children's Peace Monument. Essential historical context for understanding modern Japan.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Japanese culinary culture at the world-famous Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, and matcha treats from dozens of stalls. Join a guided family-friendly food tour to learn about Japanese ingredients, cooking traditions, and the art of sushi-making from local vendors.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Wander through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most iconic natural and cultural landscapes. Extend the adventure with a visit to Iwatayama Monkey Park, where children can hand-feed Japanese macaques with panoramic views of Kyoto below. Combine with a rickshaw ride through the historic district for a full family day.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Narita or Haneda Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer (pre-arranged limousine or Alphard van) will whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, enjoy a welcome amenity, and settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: On board or at airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: On board or at airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort — request a curated Japanese welcome platter with seasonal pickles, miso soup, and premium onigiri

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport meet-and-greet service for seamless customs and baggage handling. Confirm resort late check-in. Keep Day 1 restful to recover from jet lag.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start at the resort. Enjoy a premium Japanese breakfast with tamagoyaki, grilled fish, miso soup, and seasonal fruit at the resort's oceanfront dining room. Take a gentle stroll along the beachfront to acclimate and breathe in the sea air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area surrounding the resort. Visit a nearby Shinto shrine for a quiet cultural introduction to Japan's spiritual traditions. If the resort is coastal (Shonan, Izu, or similar region), arrange a private guided tour of the local fishing village and coastal cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a multi-course kaiseki dinner at the resort's signature restaurant. Kaiseki is Japan's haute cuisine — expect 10+ seasonal courses paired with premium sake selected by the in-house sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Full Japanese breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant
meals.lunch: Casual seaside lunch at a local premium sushi counter — try omakase nigiri with local catch
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant with sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally relaxed to ease jet lag. Book the kaiseki dinner in advance as resort fine dining often requires reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer to Tokyo (approximately 1–2 hours depending on resort location). Begin with a visit to Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple. Arrive early (by 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Walk the historic Nakamise Shopping Street for premium souvenirs including lacquerware, fans, and traditional sweets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Tsukiji Outer Market for an immersive food tour. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, premium wagyu skewers, and seasonal street food. A private guided culinary tour enhances the experience with expert commentary on Japanese food culture and market history.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a Michelin-starred restaurant in Tokyo — consider Sukiyabashi Jiro (Ginza), Saito, or a premium teppanyaki venue. Afterward, enjoy a nighttime stroll through the illuminated Ginza district.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at resort before departure or at a traditional kissaten (coffee shop) in Asakusa
meals.lunch: Tsukiji Outer Market omakase sushi experience at a premium counter
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred Japanese cuisine in Ginza — book 2–3 months in advance

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is best experienced early morning. Arrange a private English-speaking guide for both Asakusa and Tsukiji for maximum depth. Keep luggage at the hotel if day-tripping from resort.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Kyoto via the Shinkansen (bullet train) — a premium Green Car or Gran Class seat is recommended for the 2.5-hour journey. Check into a luxury ryokan in Kyoto (e.g., Tawaraya, Kyoto Okura, or Suiran). After settling in, visit Fushimi Inari Taisha — the iconic shrine with thousands of vermillion torii gates. Hike the lower trails for stunning photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Arashiyama district. Walk through the ethereal Arashiyama Bamboo Grove, one of Japan's most iconic natural landscapes. Continue to the Arashiyama Monkey Park Iwatayama for a family-friendly wildlife encounter with Japanese macaques against a panoramic Kyoto backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional kaiseki dinner at your Kyoto ryokan — served in-room by a kimono-clad attendant, followed by a soak in an in-room hinoki wood onsen bath.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at resort or on the Shinkansen (ekiben bento box — a premium train tradition)
meals.lunch: Tofu cuisine lunch at Arashiyama's Shigetsu restaurant inside Tenryu-ji temple gardens
meals.dinner: In-room kaiseki at the Kyoto ryokan — a quintessential luxury Japanese experience

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kyoto ryokan well in advance — top properties fill up months ahead, especially during cherry blossom season. Gran Class Shinkansen seats include meal service.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for the crown jewel of the trip — Cherry Blossom Viewing at Maruyama Park. Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree (shidare-zakura) is a breathtaking sight, especially in the morning light before crowds arrive. A private guide can share the history and cultural significance of hanami. Explore the adjacent Yasaka Shrine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Kinkaku-ji (the Golden Pavilion) — one of Japan's most celebrated cultural landmarks, a Zen Buddhist temple whose top floors are covered in gold leaf and reflect magnificently on the surrounding pond. Continue to Ryoan-ji Temple to contemplate Japan's most famous rock garden.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Gion district at dusk — Kyoto's historic geisha quarter. If arranged in advance, attend a private ozashiki (geisha banquet) for an unparalleled cultural immersion. Alternatively, dine at a premium Gion restaurant overlooking the Shirakawa canal.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast at the ryokan — grilled fish, rice, miso, pickles, and seasonal vegetables
meals.lunch: Obanzai (Kyoto home-style cuisine) at a refined Nishiki Market restaurant
meals.dinner: Private ozashiki banquet in Gion or a Michelin-starred Kyoto kaiseki restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Cherry blossom peak in mid-April is ideal — Maruyama Park is stunning. Book the ozashiki experience through a concierge at least 1 month in advance as access is limited.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nara — just 45 minutes from Kyoto by express train. Visit Todai-ji Temple, home to Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue (Daibutsu). Wander through Nara Park where hundreds of freely roaming sacred deer bow to visitors for shika senbei (deer crackers) — a beloved family activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kasuga Taisha, Nara's most celebrated Shinto shrine, lined with thousands of stone and bronze lanterns. Walk the peaceful Naramachi historic district with its preserved merchant townhouses. Return to Kyoto by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the ryokan with an extended onsen session. Enjoy a private in-room sake tasting curated by the ryokan's sommelier featuring premium Fushimi sake from Kyoto's famous brewing district.

meals.breakfast: Ryokan Japanese breakfast
meals.lunch: Kaiseki bento lunch at a premium Nara restaurant — try Yoshikasuga near Kasuga Taisha
meals.dinner: Light in-ryokan dinner or room service — keep it simple after a full day of exploration

day_by_day.notes: Nara's deer are gentle but persistent — keep food secured. The Todai-ji Great Buddha Hall is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Comfortable walking shoes are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Hiroshima via Shinkansen (approximately 1.5 hours from Kyoto in Green Car). Visit the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park — a profoundly moving and educational experience for the whole family. The museum chronicles the events of August 6, 1945 with extraordinary historical depth. Pay respects at the Atomic Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome), a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short ferry to Miyajima Island — one of Japan's 'Three Views.' See the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine at high tide, a truly otherworldly sight. Explore the shrine complex, encounter friendly deer, and hike partway up Mt. Misen for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hiroshima for dinner. Try Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (savory layered pancake) at a premium restaurant — Hassho is a beloved high-end option. Return to Kyoto ryokan by late evening Shinkansen.

meals.breakfast: Ryokan breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Anago (conger eel) rice bento — Miyajima's signature dish — at a premium island restaurant
meals.dinner: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki at Hassho or a premium teppan restaurant in Hiroshima

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum is deeply emotional — prepare children with age-appropriate context beforehand. Check ferry schedules to Miyajima. The floating torii is most dramatic at high tide — check tide tables in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Tokyo via Shinkansen (Gran Class). Check into a luxury Tokyo hotel (e.g., The Peninsula Tokyo, Aman Tokyo, or Park Hyatt Tokyo). Begin with a visit to the Imperial Palace East Gardens — a serene, historically significant green space in the heart of Tokyo with late cherry blossoms still possible in mid-April.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hamarikyu Gardens — a stunning Edo-period landscape garden at the mouth of the Sumida River. Take a traditional yakatabune (roofed pleasure boat) cruise along the Sumida River for a unique perspective of Tokyo's skyline and bridges.
day_by_day.evening: Ascend to the Tokyo Skytree observation deck at sunset for panoramic views of the city. Dine at a premium restaurant on the upper floors of a Tokyo skyscraper — New York Bar at Park Hyatt Tokyo (Lost in Translation fame) offers an iconic evening experience.

meals.breakfast: Gran Class Shinkansen breakfast service or hotel breakfast upon arrival
meals.lunch: Traditional tea ceremony with wagashi sweets at Hamarikyu's Nakajima no Ochaya teahouse
meals.dinner: New York Bar & Grill at Park Hyatt Tokyo — premium steaks, jazz, and iconic Tokyo views

day_by_day.notes: Gran Class on the Tokaido Shinkansen offers a premium cabin experience with meal service. Book Tokyo hotel well in advance. Hamarikyu teahouse is a hidden gem — arrive early.

day_by_day.morning: Visit teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets (depending on which has reopened) — Tokyo's world-famous immersive digital art museum. An extraordinary, multi-sensory experience beloved by families and art enthusiasts alike. Book tickets well in advance as they sell out quickly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic waterfront island. Visit the life-sized Gundam statue (family favorite), browse DiverCity Tokyo Plaza, and enjoy views of the Rainbow Bridge. Alternatively, explore the luxury boutiques of Omotesando (Tokyo's Champs-Élysées) for premium Japanese fashion and design.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a world-class Tokyo restaurant. Consider Narisawa (innovative Japanese cuisine with nature philosophy), Joel Robuchon Tokyo, or a premium wagyu sukiyaki experience at Imahan in Ginza. Celebrate the final evening with a bottle of premium Japanese whisky at a high-end bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — request a Japanese-style option with grilled fish and miso
meals.lunch: Premium ramen at Fuunji or Tsuta (Michelin-starred ramen) — a must-try luxury comfort food experience
meals.dinner: Narisawa or premium wagyu sukiyaki at Imahan Ginza — a grand farewell dinner

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets must be purchased online in advance — they frequently sell out weeks ahead. Omotesando is ideal for last-minute luxury gift shopping including Issey Miyake, Comme des Garçons, and premium Japanese ceramics.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo. Enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Take a peaceful early morning walk through Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — one of Tokyo's finest parks, often holding late cherry blossoms in April. A tranquil and beautiful final memory of Japan.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to hotel for checkout. Private luxury transfer to Narita or Haneda Airport. Allow ample time for duty-free shopping — stock up on premium Japanese whisky (Yamazaki, Hibiki), matcha confections, and luxury cosmetics.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Japan. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through the culture, history, and natural beauty of Japan.

meals.breakfast: Premium hotel breakfast — a final Japanese feast
meals.lunch: Airport premium lounge dining or a final bowl of ramen at the airport's renowned ramen street
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for Tokyo airports. Haneda is closer to central Tokyo (35 min); Narita requires 60–90 min. Use remaining yen for airport duty-free — Japan's airport shops are excellent. Consider purchasing a premium Japanese whisky set as a lasting memento.
